text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 saving banks has decided to withdraw its takeover bid for Fokus Bank. Sparebankgruppen had been widely expected to give up the attempt to acquire Fokus after it was asked by the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission to consider withdrawing the bid.

- The board of cruise company Norwegian Cruise Line (NCL) will ask shareholders at the annual general meeting for permission to issue 84 million new shares. The new capital will be used for acquire other companies.

- Children in single-parent families with their fathers have better contact with the rest of their family than children who grow up with their mothers, a Danish study shows. The study also concludes that fathers are less stressed and hit children less than women do.
- Norway's financial markets fear that a new central government could lead to more expansive financial policies than currently under the ruling Labour Party.

- Manager Sverre Skogen at Aker Maritime has not altered his forecast for the company's results this year despite higher-than-expected costs for the Njord oil platform, which it is constructing for Norsk Hydro. Aker Maritime's share price fell eight percent on Wednesday after it announced the extra expenses.
